subject: industrial-systems
audience: FE Industrial & Systems candidates and industrial engineering students
title: The Process With Cp 1.67 That Still Had Cpk 0.67
featured_title: THE PROCESS WITH CP 1.67 THAT STILL HAD CPK 0.67

presentation.challenge: The process spread fit comfortably inside the specification width, but the mean had shifted toward the USL. Cp looked strong while Cpk exposed the centering problem.

practice.primary_question: How do Cp and Cpk differ when a process is not centered between its specification limits?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Using Cp alone to declare a process capable even when the process mean is shifted close to one specification limit.

case_dna.target_misconception: If Cp is greater than one, the process is necessarily capable regardless of where its mean lies.
case_dna.why_plausible: Cp compares total specification width with six sigma, so it can look favorable without showing process centering.
case_dna.corrected_model: Cp measures potential capability from spread only; Cpk also accounts for process centering by using the smaller distance from the mean to a specification limit.

problem_statement: A process has specifications 9.5 to 10.5 mm, mean μ=10.3 mm, and standard deviation σ=0.10 mm. A quality report calculates Cp=(10.5-9.5)/(6×0.10)=1.67 and concludes that the process is highly capable. Determine Cp and Cpk and explain why the conclusion is incomplete.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The process width looked good, but the mean was not centered.
gates.prompt: Which capability index accounts for centering?

options.label: Use Cp for spread and Cpk for spread plus centering
options.reason: Cpk uses the nearest specification limit and therefore penalizes a shifted mean.

options.label: Cp alone proves actual capability
options.reason: Cp does not use the process mean.

options.label: Cp and Cpk are always equal
options.reason: They are equal only when the process is centered between the specifications.

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Measure the nearest specification margin
gates.running_label: COMPARING MEAN TO BOTH SPEC LIMITS…
gates.result: Cpk is about 0.67 because the mean is close to the USL.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove Cpk
gates.success: Upper-side index=0.667 and lower-side index=2.667, so Cpk=0.667.
gates.hint: Use the smaller of the upper- and lower-side capability ratios.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: Cp and Cpk answer different questions

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the capability report
report: C3. Since Cp>1, the process is centered and capable.

claims.label: C2
claims.reason: This is the stated process mean.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: Cp does not measure centering, and Cpk is only about 0.67.

evidence_choices.label: Cpk=min(0.67,2.67)=0.67
evidence_choices.reason: The upper specification margin controls actual capability.

correction.template: The process has Cp={cp} but Cpk={cpk}, revealing a centering problem.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Recenter the process without changing variation
gates.constraint: Keep σ=0.10 mm and specifications 9.5 to 10.5 mm.

options.label: Center μ at 10.0 mm, giving Cpk=1.67
options.reason: Both specification margins become 0.5 mm, so Cpk=0.5/0.30=1.67.

options.label: Shift μ to 10.5 mm
options.reason: That places the mean directly at the USL and drives Cpk to zero.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Evaluate another process
gates.prompt: For LSL=24.5, USL=25.5, μ=25.1, and σ=0.10, what is Cpk?

options.reason: That is Cp, which ignores the 0.1 shift from center.
That is only the lower-side capability ratio.

gates.explanation: Cpk is controlled by the nearer specification limit.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the capability analysis
gates.confirmation: I confirm that Cp measures potential capability from process spread while Cpk also reflects how well the process is centered.

items.label: What failed
items.value: A favorable Cp was treated as proof of actual centered capability.

items.label: What was missed
items.value: The process mean was shifted close to the upper specification limit.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Use both Cp and Cpk; Cpk is governed by the nearest specification limit.

seo.seo_title: Process Capability Cp vs Cpk Off-Center Process | FE E-088
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Industrial & Systems Case E-088: Cp is 1.67 but Cpk is only 0.67 because the process mean is shifted toward the USL.
seo.focus_keyphrase: FE Industrial process capability Cp Cpk
seo.excerpt: A process can have a strong Cp and a weak Cpk when its variation is small but its mean is poorly centered.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Cp and Cpk?
faqs.a: Cp measures potential capability from spread; Cpk also accounts for process centering.

faqs.q: When are Cp and Cpk equal?
faqs.a: When the process mean is centered between the upper and lower specification limits.
